plots.brief: Customs house, about 13x11 walls, two storeys on a stone-brick plinth at y 65, fronting Harbour Street (door north under a small calcite portico). Diorite and calcite walls, deepslate roof, tall mullioned windows, a blue banner and a scales-and-seal sign; a barred spruce loading hatch on the south face toward the warehouses.

Fish market hall, about 15x10, open-sided: stone-brick piers and a long dark-slate roof on spruce posts, stone slab counters with barrels and cauldrons of water, a gutter channel down the middle of the floor. Open to Harbour Street on the north; hanging lanterns and a fish-shaped weathervane on the ridge.

Sailors' chapel on the spur's north rise at y 74, about 9x11 walls with a nave and a small apse toward the lake (south). Calcite and stone brick on a chiselled plinth, steep deepslate roof, a slender oxidised-copper spirelet with a ship weathervane, stained-glass blue windows; door north under a small gabled porch with a hanging ship's bell. Steps climb up from Harbour Street.

Harbourmaster's house on the eastern shoulder of the spur at y 71, about 9x9 walls, two storeys, stone-brick base and diorite walls, dark roof, door north to Harbour Street under a spruce porch; chart-room bay window looking to the lake, a signal mast with flags on the roof and a stone retaining wall on the downhill side.

The ropewalk: a long low shed about 20x6 walls, one storey, open slatted spruce sides, stone-brick end piers, a long dark roof with a lantern vent; rope-twisting frames and coils inside, door north on Harbour Street, a drying yard of posts along the south wall.

Sailors' lodgings, about 14x11 walls, two storeys with a row of small dormers, whitewashed diorite on a stone plinth at y 63, spruce door north on Harbour Street with a lantern and a ship's-lantern sign; shuttered windows, a chimney stack, dormitory beds upstairs.

Ship chandler's shop, about 7x7 walls, two storeys, shop front with a wide shuttered window and a hanging anchor sign, door east onto the harbour avenue; coils of rope, barrels and lanterns on display under a plank awning. Whitewashed diorite on a stone plinth, dark roof.

The Harbour: a walled stone quay about 35x16 whose east end meets the harbour avenue at y 63, its south half over the lake. Stone-brick quay wall on a cut-stone plinth, two spruce piers running south into the water with bollards and lanterns, a lake gate (arched, with portcullis and blue banners) at the south end, a hoist crane of spruce on the east quay, stone steps down to the waterline. Working and plain, not ornate; a copper-capped harbour-master's booth at the landward east corner by the avenue.
